title: Collapse Repeats Into #
statement:
You are given a string `s`. Split it into maximal **runs** of equal consecutive characters (for example `aaaaabcccccd` consists of the runs `aaaaa`, `b`, `ccccc`, `d`).

Build a new string by processing the runs from left to right:

- A run of length `2` or more is replaced by a single `#`.
- A run of length exactly `1` (a character with no equal neighbour) is kept unchanged.

Characters are case-sensitive, so `a` and `A` are different. The input never contains `#`. Print the resulting string.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string `s`.
outputFormat: Print the transformed string on one line.
constraints: `s` consists of English letters (upper and lower case) and digits only

examples.explanation: The runs are `aaaaa`, `b`, `ccccc`, `d`. The two long runs become `#`, while `b` and `d` stay as they are.
Every run has length 1, so nothing changes.
`aa` becomes `#`, `bbb` becomes `#`. The last two characters are `A` and `a`, which differ in case, so both are single runs and are kept.

hints: Walk through the string and, at each position, find how far the run of equal characters extends.
Only the length of each run matters: length 1 keeps the character, length at least 2 emits one `#`.
Collect the pieces in a list and join once at the end instead of concatenating strings repeatedly.
